name: Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD)
description: Configure RBCD on a target computer by writing msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity. Requires GenericWrite or WriteDACL on the target computer object.

examples.label: Set RBCD from attacker to target

recommended.note: Find GenericWrite on computer object first

notes: Requires: GenericWrite on target, machine account quota > 0, computer account you own. Machine accounts end with $.

defense.why_it_works: Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD) is configured on the resource side: the msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity attribute on the target computer specifies which principals can delegate to it. If an attacker has GenericWrite/GenericAll on a computer account, they can set this attribute to include a computer they control, then use S4U2Self + S4U2Proxy to impersonate any user (including DA) to the target host.
defense.prerequisites: GenericWrite or GenericAll over a target computer account in AD. Control of a computer account (create via MachineAccountQuota or use a compromised workstation). Rubeus for S4U operations. NTLM hash or password of the controlled computer account.
defense.impact: T1558 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets. Impersonates any user including DA to the target computer. Produces a valid service ticket that can be used for lateral movement to the target. Works even against protected accounts via S4U2Self altservice trick.
defense.detection:
Modification of msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity on computer accounts — Event 5136 (AD object attribute changed) on the target computer object. MDI: 'Suspicious RBCD modification'. S4U2Proxy TGS requests following the attribute modification. SIEM: Event 5136 on computer object with msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity change.
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: Event 5136: msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity modified on target computer | MDI: RBCD abuse alert | Event 4769: S4U TGS request following modification | Event 4741 or 4742: computer account created/modified as the delegation principal
defense.prevention:
Set MachineAccountQuota to 0 (default is 10 — allows any user to add 10 computer accounts): Set-ADDomain -Identity corp.local -Replace @{'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota'=0}. Audit GenericWrite/GenericAll ACEs on computer objects via BloodHound. Monitor Event 5136 for computer object attribute changes. MDI deployment.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Use an already-compromised computer account instead of creating a new one (avoids computer account creation events). Set and use the RBCD ticket quickly, then revert the attribute to remove evidence.
defense.misconfiguration: MachineAccountQuota > 0 (any domain user can add computer accounts). GenericWrite on computer objects for non-admin groups. No monitoring of msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity modifications.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# MachineAccountQuota allows any user to create computer accounts (default = 10):
(Get-ADDomain).MillionBytesPerSecond  # wrong attr
Get-ADObject (Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName -Properties 'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota' | Select-Object 'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota'
# ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota : 10 → any domain user can add 10 computer accounts

# GenericWrite on a computer object:
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity 'SERVER01$' -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericWrite'}
defense.secure_config:
# Set MachineAccountQuota to 0:
Set-ADDomain -Identity corp.local -Replace @{'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota' = 0}

# Verify:
(Get-ADDomain corp.local).'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota'  # Should be 0

# Remove GenericWrite ACEs on computer objects:
# Audit with BloodHound: 'Find Computers where Domain Users can RDP' / custom ACL queries

# Monitor RBCD attribute changes:
# Enable DS Access auditing → Event 5136
# SIEM: EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity' → CRITICAL ALERT
